# Regenerating the search gold file

`../search_gold.bin` is what gammonNet's **C reference** answers for every decision in
`../search_corpus.bin`, at the canonical configuration: prune `k=12`, filter `(0,1,3)`.

It is read verbatim by `TestSearchMatchesTheGoldFile`. Recomputing both sides from a seed
would establish nothing if the two implementations had drifted apart, so the reference must
actually be built and run.

**Regenerating is a deliberate act.** Do it when — and only when — the pinned gammonNet
version changes. A gold file that moves on its own turns the parity gate into a comparison of
two moving targets.

## What you need

- a checkout of [gammonNet](https://github.com/kevung/gammonNet) at the pinned version
  (currently **v1.0.1**), including `vendor/backgammon-ai-engine` (fetched by its
  `tools/fetch_vendor.py`);
- a C compiler; nothing else. This never runs in CI.

## The two files, and the order they are made in

1. **The corpus first.** It is generated by Go, so that both sides provably answer the same
   questions:

   ```sh
   cd <blunderDB>
   BLUNDERDB_WRITE_CORPUS=1 go test ./pkg/blunderdb/engine/gammonnet/ -run TestWriteGoldCorpus
   ```

   `TestGoldCorpusIsInSync` fails if the committed corpus stops matching `buildCorpus()` —
   that guard is the whole reason the corpus is a file rather than a seed.

2. **Then the gold**, from that exact corpus:

   ```sh
   GN=<gammonNet checkout>
   V=$GN/vendor/backgammon-ai-engine
   M=<blunderDB>/pkg/blunderdb/engine/gammonnet

   gcc -O3 -march=native -I$GN/src -I$V/c_inference -I$V/c_engine -o gold gold.c \
       $GN/src/gn_search.c $GN/src/gn_infer_reference.c $GN/src/gn_encoding.c \
       $GN/src/gn_rules_reference.c $GN/src/gn_met.c $GN/src/gn_cube.c \
       $GN/src/gn_bearoff.c $GN/src/gn_evalcache.c $GN/src/gn_choose.c \
       $V/c_inference/nn_eval.c $V/c_engine/bg_engine.c -lm

   ./gold $M/testdata/search_corpus.bin \
          $M/strehl-prob5-512-512-256-128_v1.0.1_2026-08-27.bin \
          $M/strehl-prune-32_v1.0.1_2026-08-27.bin \
          $M/testdata/search_gold.bin
   ```

   About five seconds for the 85 cases — the C evaluates in batches of 32, which is why it is
   an order of magnitude faster than the Go port on the 2-ply cases (see ADR-0011 and #133).

## What the gate asserts, and what it deliberately does not

- The **same number of candidates**, the **same chosen move**, and equities agreeing to
  **1e-6**. Measured on v1.0.1: **max|Δ| = 7.153e-07** over the 85 decisions, and the chosen
  move matched in every one.
- **Two plays whose equities agree to within 1e-6 are treated as interchangeable.** The
  reference orders candidates with `qsort`, which is not stable and whose implementation has
  changed across libc versions: on an exact tie the play it returns depends on the C library
  that produced the file. A gate must not encode that. As of v1.0.1 this allowance is never
  used — the count of such ties is reported by the test, and a number that starts growing is
  itself a signal.

## The margin, and why it is worth watching

7.153e-07 against a 1e-6 tolerance is a factor of **1.4**, where network parity alone
(`reference.bin`) leaves a factor of 16 — 5.960e-08. The search accumulates thousands of
evaluations, each carrying up to one ulp of difference from the final sigmoid, so the error
grows with the tree. **At 3 or 4 ply the tolerance may not hold**, and the corpus deliberately
stops at 2, which is the canonical depth. Deepening the corpus means re-establishing the
tolerance first, not assuming it.
